summary: Built 1940 as an L-4 cabin on a timber tower on Clayton Mountain; gone, with nothing left at the site, per the register.

facts.design: L-4 cabin on a timber tower
facts.status_note: Register gives no removal date and says nothing remains at the site.

access.note: The summit is reached by the Blackwater Fire Memorial trail, a National Recreation Trail. No closure appears in these sources.

visit.trail_note: The trail starts near the Blackwater recreation resort and the Firefighter Memorial on the North Fork of the Shoshone River, and ends with a steep climb.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Shoshone National Forest

events.note: Register dates the cabin on a timber tower to 1940
Forest Service recommended renaming Double Mountain for Ranger Clayton; the 1940 report quotes the name change
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register on March 14, 2022

notes_for_editor: Built 1940 and gone are consistent across the register, the Wyoming list and the trail guide. Staffing, the removal date and the summit's condition today are not in any source read, so they are left out. The 1940 Shoshone report is read only as quoted on the register page. The register's '20 timber tower' looks garbled, so no height is given. Access is marked public from the trail guide and the designation; no closure was found.
